services.title: How we work together
services.subtitle: Three ways to start. All three end in something running in production, not a PDF.

items.name: AI audit
items.summary: Your team wants to use AI but nobody knows where to start — or there's a prototype that never quite ships.
bullets: I review the product, the data, and the current stack
I identify where an LLM pays for itself — and where it doesn't
Cost, latency, and risk estimates per use case
items.outcome: Deliverable: a prioritized plan with the first feature ready to build.

items.name: AI feature to production
items.summary: You know what you want to build. You need someone to take it from idea to something that survives real users.
bullets: Prompt, context, and evaluation design
Integration with your backend and UI, streaming included
Guardrails, rate limiting, and cost control
items.outcome: Deliverable: the feature in production, with your team able to maintain it.

items.name: Ongoing technical advisory
items.summary: You have an engineering team and need AI judgment without adding a senior head count.
bullets: Architecture review and model decisions
Code review and pairing with your team
Async availability plus a weekly session
items.outcome: Deliverable: your team making better calls without waiting on me.

services.note: Your case doesn't fit any of these? Reach out anyway — the first call is free and exists to find out whether this makes sense.

about.title: About Me
about.bio: AI Tech Lead and consultant with 8+ years shipping production software. I lead AI engineering at WotDev and advise companies on putting AI into real products — deciding where an LLM actually earns its place, then taking it from prototype to production. Deep on Python and Django on the backend, React and Next.js on the front. Before that I built at scale: sports streaming on Apple TV (SNY, FanDuel) and global travel platforms (Lonely Planet). Based in Lima, Peru, working globally.
